CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  OCTOBER 23, 2023
  MISSION STATEMENT

  The City of Alhambra is dedicated to responsive, creative leadership and
  quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a supportive
  business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our
  community.

Watch and listen to the meeting as follows:
Zoom Webinar direct link:
https://cityofalhambra-org.zoom.us/j/81321778489?pwd=YU1BTWtqSXpNeEo1MWFSME1mZ1FmUT09
Webinar ID: 813 2177 8489, Passcode: 644586
Or by telephone by dialing (833) 548-0276 (Toll Free) or (833) 548-0282 (Toll Free) or (877) 853-5257
(Toll Free) or (888) 475-4499 (Toll Free) or +1(719) 359-4580 or +1(309) 205-3325 or +1(253) 215-8782
or +1(346) 248-7799 or +1(646) 931-3860 or +1(301) 715-8592 or +1(312) 626-6799 or +1(646) 558-8656
and entering Webinar ID: 813 2177 8489 and Passcode: 644586. Please Note: All members of the public
calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that the meeting can proceed. Meetings can also be
viewed via livestream here: https://www.spectrumstream.com/streaming/alhambra/live.cfm
Addressing the Council:
In person: Section 2.04.210 of the Alhambra Municipal Code establishes the procedures for addressing
the Council. Any person wishing to address the Council during the meeting should complete a Speaker
Request Card and submit it to the City Clerk so the City Council knows you wish to speak. When called
upon by the presiding officer, please step to the podium.
Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the “Raise Hand”
function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will unmute speakers
participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your time to speak.
Remarks are limited to 5 minutes; however, the presiding officer may either extend or reduce the maximum
time to such period of time as the Council may determine.

Standards of Decorum: Any person addressing the Council who refuses to stop speaking after his/her
time has expired or any person who behaves in such a manner as to interfere with or impede the progress
of the City Council meeting who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior
may be removed from the City Council chambers upon direction of the presiding officer.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or his/her designee, shall be Sergeant-at-Arms of the
Council meetings. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the presiding
officer for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the Council meeting.

Persons Authorized to be Within Rail: No person, except City official or their designees, shall be
permitted within the rail in front of the Council Chamber without the express consent of the Council.

Agenda Tracking Numbers: All numbers listed in bold after the title of each Agenda item are City Clerk
tracking numbers that are used for filing and research purposes.

   CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AGENDA
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  October 23, 2023
  6:00 p.m.
  ROLL CALL:
  COUNCIL:  Lee, Maloney, Pérez, Andrade-Stadler, Maza

  FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to
prioritize respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples
throughout California, especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with
respect and gratitude for the Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the
caretakers of this land. It is through their examples that we are reminded of our greater
responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take care of each other.

COUNCIL BUSINESS

1.  REQUEST FOR COUNCILMEMBER PARTICIPATION VIA VIDEO/TELECONFERENCE
  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54953(F) – F2M23-7, M2M23-180

  On October 9, 2023, Councilmember Andrade-Stadler requested that her Council
  colleagues vote to allow her participation via video/teleconference at the October 23, 2023
  City Council meeting due to medical reasons. Under current Government Code section
  54953(f), this is allowable action if approved by the City Council.

  Recommended Action:  City Council consider approving Councilmember Andrade-
  Stadler’s request by motion and vote to allow her to participate and vote remotely via
  video/teleconference in City Council meetings due to an emergency medical reason under
  Government Code Section 54953(f). (M2M23-180)

READING OF ORDINANCE TITLES

Government Code Section 36934 requires that all ordinances be read in full prior to City Council
taking action on the ordinance. By listing the ordinance title on the Council agenda, Council may
determine that the title has been read.

Recommended Action:  By motion, determine that the titles to all ordinances which appear
on this public agenda have been read, and waive further reading.

  2
10-23-23
 PUBLIC HEARING

2.  CONSIDER ADOPTION OF AN URGENCY INTERIM ZONING ORDINANCE
  EXTENDING ORDINANCE NO. O2M23-4818, THE PROHIBITION ON THE
  ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW FIREARM SALES BUSINESSES AND DETERMINE THIS
  ACTION IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA – F2M23-7, N2M23-124, O2M23-4818, O2M23-4821

  This is the time and place set by Notice No. N2M23-124 for the City Council to hold a
  public hearing to consider adoption of an urgency interim zoning ordinance extending
  Ordinance No. O2M23-4818, the prohibition on the establishment of new firearm sales
  businesses. At the September 25, 2023 City Council meeting, the City Council adopted
  Ordinance No. O2M23-4818 imposing a 45-day moratorium on the establishment of new
  retail firearm sales businesses in the City. The reasoning behind and need for such
  ordinance is set forth in the September 25, 2023 staff report and ordinance. Staff requires
  additional time to study the “buffer” ordinance that Monterey Park adopted and evaluate
  its suitability for the City of Alhambra, then prepare a recommendation to the Planning
  Commission, and ultimately the City Council. California Government Code section 65858
  allows for the adoption of interim zoning regulations, including moratorium ordinances, on
  an urgency basis to preserve the health, safety and welfare of the residents of Alhambra
  by maintaining the status quo while research and analysis is undertaken to develop
  appropriate regulations to discuss these concerns. An initial ordinance can be adopted to
  last 45 days. Thereafter, the ordinance can be extended, if needed, for a period of ten
  months and 15 days. This ordinance would extend the current ordinance to and through
  September 24, 2024. If permanent regulations are adopted prior to the expiration of the
  extended moratorium, it can be repealed at that time.

  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of this extension Ordinance under the
  California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”)
  and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq.,
  the “CEQA Guidelines”). This Ordinances is not subject to further review environmental
  review because: (1) it will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical
  change in the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15060(c)(2); (2) there is no possibility
  that the Ordinance itself may have a significant effect on the environment (14 Cal. Code
  Regs. § 15061(b)(3)); and (3) the Ordinance, by itself, does not constitute a “project” as
  defined in the CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15378). The Ordinance is for
  general policies and procedure-making.

  Recommended Action:  City Council:

  1.  Conduct a public hearing; and,

  2.  Consider adopting by a 4/5 vote:

  Ordinance No. O2M23-4821: An Urgency Ordinance of the City
  Council of the City of Alhambra, California, enacted pursuant to
  California Government Code Section 65858, extending Ordinance No.
  O2M23-4818, an interim zoning ordinance temporarily prohibiting the
  establishment of new firearm sales businesses in the City

  3
10-23-23
 PRESENTATIONS

3.  TRANSPORTATION PRESENTATIONS:

  a.  MOBILITY SURVEY RESULTS – F2M23-72

  Over the last several weeks, a mobility survey has been underway to help the City
  better ascertain mobility preferences and needs throughout Alhambra and
  opinions on how to shape local transportation. True North Research Inc.
  conducted the random survey, which results shall be presented to the City Council
  for consideration as the City continues to evaluate and undertake transportation
  planning, projects and programs. Approximately 600 interviews were conducted.

  b.  ALHAMBRA COMMUNITY TRANSIT (ACT) BUS RIDERSHIP EXPANSION –
  F2M23-16

  The City of Alhambra contracts the operation of the Alhambra Community Transit
  (ACT), a fixed route shuttle bus service that operates within the City limits. On
  June 26, 2023, Martin Gombert from Mobility Advancement presented the initial
  results of Route and Ridership Study. Based on the feedback received from the
  City Council, Mr. Gombert will present options to increase ridership and provide
  service to areas of Alhambra south of the 10 freeway.

  c.  LOCAL ROADWAY SAFETY PROGRAM – F2M23-68

  The City of Alhambra received a State grant from Caltrans to prepare a Local
  Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP). Darryl DePencier with Kimley-Horn will present how
  the LRSP provides the City with a framework for systematic infrastructure
  improvements to reduce or eliminate safety issues identified by the plan. Further,
  the LRSP enables the City to apply for grant funding through the Highway Safety
  Improvement Program. The LRSP was prepared in conformance with Federal and
  State standards.

  d.  BIKE AND PEDESTRIAN IMPROVEMENT PLAN:  PROJECT UPDATE –
  F2M22-33

  On October 10, 2023, staff and Alta Planning met with the City Council
  Subcommittee on the latest developments of the City’s Bike and Pedestrian
  Improvement Plan. The plan is near completion. Alta Planning will present a
  summary of the project timeline; the proposed bicycle network, classifications and
  phasing options; pedestrian recommendations and treatments; discussion
  regarding demonstrations and pilots; programs and policies to undertake; plan
  implementation cost estimates; and, next steps.

  Recommended Action:  City Council receive and file these informational reports (a-
  d) and provide direction to staff as deemed appropriate.

4.  COMPREHENSIVE ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY PLAN: PROJECT UPDATE
  – F2M22-64

  4
10-23-23
   On October 10, 2023, staff and Environmental Science Associates (ESA) Consulting met
  with the City Council Subcommittee on the Comprehensive Environmental Sustainability
  Plan to address progress and next steps. Staff will present a summary of the meeting’s
  highlights including reference to the scope of work and focus areas, schedule, and
  community engagement.

  Recommended Action:  City Council receive and file this informational report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 5 – 19)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda are considered by the City Council to be routine and
will be enacted by one motion unless a citizen or Council member requests otherwise; in which
case, the item will be removed for separate consideration.

5.  NIB: 2023 ALLEY REHABILITATION PROJECT (AREA A / PHASE I) – F2M23-67,
  N2M23-126

  The 2023 Alley Rehabilitation Project consists of 8 alley segments, with an additional 2
  alley segments for alternate bids within City boundaries. The alley segments are
  categorized as failed condition. Staff has prepared specifications for distribution to
  qualified firms to submit proposals for the preparation of PS&E documents. The project is
  located between Ethel Avenue on the West, Valley Boulevard on the South, Atlantic
  Boulevard on the East, and Front Street on the North. The exact location of the project is
  outlined in the staff report.

  Recommended Action:  City Council authorize the circulation of a Notice Inviting
  Bids to prospective contractors for the 2023 Alley Rehabilitation Project (Area A / Phase
  I) with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on November 16, 2023; and, direct staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

6.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF FOUR POLICE PATROL VEHICLES – F2M23-
  6A, C2M23-81, M2M23-181

  The FY 2023-2024 budget includes the replacement of police patrol vehicles. Staff is
  seeking to purchase four police patrol vehicles to replace the aging vehicles through a
  cooperative purchase agreement. Cooperative purchase is allowable per Alhambra
  Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On September 15, 2021, Sourcewell opened four bids for
  the procurement of vehicles, cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with related equipment,
  accessories, and services. Sourcewell awarded contract 091521-NAF to National Auto
  Fleet Group on November 4, 2021 - a contract that does not expire until November 8,
  2025. Per the Sourcewell bid specifications, there is the option of purchasing police
  vehicles. Staff is recommending purchasing four police vehicles utilizing this option.

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group for the
  purchase of four police patrol vehicles in the amount of $201,528.68; and, direct staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-181)

  5
10-23-23
 7.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF FOUR UTILITY WORK TRUCKS – F2M23-6A,
  C2M23-82, M2M23-182

  The FY 2023-24 budget includes the replacement of four utility service body trucks for the
  Public Works and Utilities Department. The utility trucks to be replaced are old and have
  exceeded their expected useful life. Staff is seeking to purchase the utility body trucks
  through a cooperative purchase agreement. Cooperative purchase is allowable per
  Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On September 15, 2021, Sourcewell opened
  four bids for the procurement of vehicles, cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with related
  equipment, accessories, and services. Sourcewell awarded contract 091521-NAF to
  National Auto Fleet Group on November 4, 2021 - a contract that does not expire until
  November 8, 2025. Per the Sourcewell bid specifications, there is the option of purchasing
  vehicles and related accessories. Staff is recommending purchasing four utility work trucks
  utilizing this option.

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group for the
  purchase of four utility work trucks in the amount of $286,236.52; and, direct staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-182)

8.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON MARENGO AVENUE – F2M23-66,
  RFP2M23-23, C2M23-83, M2M23-183

  On September 11, 2023, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for
  Proposals for Professional Engineering Design Services for the Water Main Replacement
  Project on Marengo Avenue. The 10-inch cast iron water main on Marengo Avenue
  between Grand Avenue and Alhambra Road was installed in 1966. Replacing the water
  main would greatly improve flow, firefighting capabilities, and overall system reliability.
  Staff reviewed a total of three proposals. Elie Farah, Inc. was selected based on their
  distinguished qualifications, experience, reputation, responsiveness, availability, and cost.

  Recommended Action:  City Council award a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  Elie Farah, Inc. for Professional Engineering Design Services for the Water Main
  Replacement Project on Marengo Avenue in an amount not to exceed $24,305; and, direct
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-183)

9.  NIB: PURCHASE OF MOTOROLA MOBILE  RADIOS  FOR  THE  POLICE
  DEPARTMENT – F2M23-6B, N2M23-128

  Police operations rely heavily on mobile radios (radios installed into patrol vehicles), which
  are critical for ensuring safe and effective service to the community. The Police
  Department fleet currently uses Motorola XTL 5000 radios which were purchased over ten
  years ago and have exceeded their end-of-life expectancy. Additionally, these radios are
  no longer supported by the manufacturer. Procuring new mobile radios is a vital measure
  towards enhancing and modernizing the Police Department communication system to
  meet the community’s safety needs.

  6
10-23-23
   Recommended Action:  City Council authorize staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids
  to prospective contractors for the purchase of Motorola mobile radios for the Police
  Department; and, direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

10.  APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT FOR POLICE PURSUIT MITIGATION TECHNOLOGY –
  F2M23-69, C2M23-84, M2M23-184

  Staff requests that the City Council approve a contract between the City of Alhambra and
  StarChase GPS Solutions for the use of pursuit mitigation technology. StarChase has
  created modern-day technology that reduces risk in vehicle pursuits that has proven
  effective in enhancing public safety, mitigating liability and increasing the apprehension
  rate of fleeing suspects. The technology provides the option to deploy a GPS projectile
  onto a vehicle that has been identified as having been used in a crime. StarChase is the
  only law enforcement tool (vehicle mounted/installed and hand-held device) of its kind that
  allows a police officer to tag and track a suspect vehicle from a distance in virtually any
  situation.

  Recommended Action:  City Council approve a contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  StarChase GPS Solutions for the use of pursuit mitigation technology in an amount not to
  exceed $89,741.24 over a three-year period; authorize the Chief of Police to execute said
  contract; and, direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.
  (M2M23-184)

11.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTING SERVICES TO DEVELOP THE
  LOCAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN – F2M23-70, RFP2M23-25

  Staff applied for a Hazard Mitigation Grant Program grant in the amount of $135,450 with
  a match commitment of $15,050. The grant application was approved for funding. On
  October 9, 2023, the City Council accepted the grant. Staff is seeking to solicit proposals
  for a firm to provide professional consulting services to develop Alhambra’s Local Hazard
  Mitigation Plan as outlined in 44 CFR Part 201 and pursuant to the Federal Emergency
  Management Agency’s current hazard mitigation plan guidance.

  Recommended Action:  City Council authorize the distribution of a Request for
  Proposals to qualified firms to develop the City of Alhambra Local Hazard Mitigation Plan;
  and, direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

12.  AUTHORIZE RFP: BILLING SERVICES – F2M23-71, RFP2M23-26

  Community Risk Reduction (CRR) is a division of the Fire Department with staff dedicated
  to increasing safety, preventing or reducing fire losses and ensuring compliance with
  applicable codes and ordinances. Conducting regular fire, life safety and environmental
  inspections are also functions of the CRR division. The Fire Department is seeking a
  qualified firm with extensive experience to provide billing management, invoicing and
  customer service.

  7
10-23-23
   Recommended Action:  City Council authorize the distribution of a Request for
  Proposals to qualified firms for Community Risk Reduction (CRR) billing services; and,
  direct staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

13.  AUTHORIZING  RESOLUTION  FOR  GRANT  APPLICATION(S) UNDER
  CALRECYCLE’S SB 1383 LOCAL ASSISTANCE GRANT PROGRAM – F2M23-18,
  R2M23-52

  The Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) offers the SB 1383
  Local Assistance Grant Program to provide funding to local jurisdictions to assist with the
  implementation of regulation requirements associated with SB 1383. The City of Alhambra
  is implementing various measures to achieve the state-mandated waste diversion goals.
  For the current cycle of the SB 1383 Local Assistance Grant Program, the tentative funding
  estimate for the City is $152,477.

  Recommended Action:  City Council approve the submittal of application(s) to the
  Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) SB 1383 Local
  Assistance Grant Program; adopt Resolution No. R2M23-52 entitled: A Resolution of the
  City Council of the City of Alhambra authorizing submittal of application(s) to CalRecyle
  for the SB 1383 Local Assistance Grant Program, enabling the submittal of such
  application(s) to CalRecycle; and, direct and authorize staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize the Council’s action.

14.  2023 STRATEGIC PLAN UPDATE – F2M23-35

  On April 24, 2023, the City Council approved the 2023 Strategic Plan following two special
  City Council meetings that were conducted to review and update the goals and objectives
  that were previously established in the 2021 Strategic Plan. Subsequently, on July 24,
  2023, staff provided the first update to the 2023 Strategic Plan. Staff is now and will
  continue to present quarterly updates to the Council and will diligently work through
  Strategic Plan goals and individual items to enable important progress.

  Recommended Action:  City Council receive and file the Alhambra Strategic Plan
  update.

15.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT FOR PROFESSIONAL OUTREACH SERVICES TO
  ADVANCE THE SR-710 TERMINUS CONCEPT PROJECT AND APPROPRIATE
  FUNDS – F2M19-32, C2M20-42, M2M23-185

  The City of Alhambra has been working with Advocacy since 2020 for community outreach
  subject to the City’s work to advance the SR-710 Terminus concepts, which efforts include
  stakeholder and community meetings and updates via the Advancing Alhambra website.
  The original contract amount was for $200,000 and includes an option to extend services
  through 2025. Staff is seeking to retain the contract with Advocacy for ongoing project
  outreach, particularly as the City’s SR-710 Terminus concepts advance. The contract
  performance by Advocacy has been satisfactory to the needs of the City.

  8
10-23-23
   Recommended Action:  City Council approve an amendment, subject to final
  language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to the agreement with
  Advocacy (C2M20-42) for ongoing community outreach specific to the SR-710 Terminus
  Project; authorize the contract term through August 26, 2024; authorize an additional
  $25,000 in contract costs and appropriations; and, direct staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-185)

16.  TREASURER’S REPORT – F2M23-1
  Recommended Action:  City Council receive and file as submitted the Treasurer's
  Report prepared by the Director of Finance for the month of September 30, 2023, listing
  all of the City's investments as of September 30, 2023.

17.  PERSONNEL ACTIONS – F2M23-2

  Recommended Action:  City Council ratify the actions of the City Manager set forth
  in that certain Personnel Actions document dated October 23, 2023 showing the various
  appointments, classifications, salary changes, etc., since the last City Council meeting.

18.  DEMANDS - F2M23-1

  Recommended Action:  City Council approve as submitted Final Check List (8645
  thru 8678) in the amount of $1,884.09 for the period ending August 22, 2023; Final Check
  List (242135 thru 242165) in the amount of $2,078,842.32 for the period ending August
  24, 2023; Final Check List (242166 thru 242302) in the amount of $922,448.26 for the
  period ending August 24, 2023 and Schedule of Wire Transfers in the amount of
  $2,706,969.16 for the week ending August 18, 2023; Final Check List (242303 thru
  242320) in the amount of $102,732.78 for the period ending August 31, 2023 and
  Schedule of Wire Transfers in the amount of $2,113,935.57 for the week ending August
  31, 2023; Final Check List (242321 thru 242420) in the amount of $385,236.43 for the
  period ending August 31, 2023; and, Final Check List (242421 thru 242589) in the amount
  of $62,196.92 for the period ending September 5, 2023.

19.  FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE EXTENDING THE TERM OF ORDINANCE NO.
  O2M23-4812, A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON CERTAIN “NO FAULT”
  RESIDENTIAL EVICTIONS DUE TO A PROPERTY OWNER’S INTENT TO
  SUBSTANTIALLY REMODEL THE TENANT’S UNIT IN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  AND DETERMINE THIS ACTION IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA – F2M23-7, O2M23-4812,
  O2M23-4822

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M23-4812, imposing a
  temporary moratorium on so called “renovictions,” through December 31, 2023. On
  September 30, 2023, SB 567 was signed by the Governor. SB 567 revises certain tenant
  protections in State law which address the concerns that the City’s moratorium was
  intended to address. However, those protections do not take effect until April 1, 2024. At
  the October 9, 2023 City Council meeting, the City Council directed that an amendment
  to Ordinance No. O2M23-4812 be agendized to extend the term of the temporary
  9
10-23-23
   moratorium on renovictions until the tenant protections of SB 567 become effective. The
  City reviewed the environmental impacts of this Ordinance under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the
  regulations promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA
  Guidelines”). This Ordinance is not subject to further review environmental review
  because: (1) it will not result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change
  in the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15060(c)(2); (2) there is no possibility that this
  Ordinance themselves may have a significant effect on the environment (14 Cal. Code
  Regs. § 15061(b)(3)); and (3) the Ordinance, by itself, do not constitute a “project” as
  defined in the CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15378). The Ordinance is for
  general policies and procedure-making.

  Recommended Action:  Declare introduced for its first reading the following
  ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M23-4822: An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  Alhambra, California, extending the term of Ordinance No. O2M23-4812, a
  temporary Moratorium on certain “no fault” residential evictions due to a
  property owner’s intent to substantially remodel the tenant’s unit in the City of
  Alhambra

  which ordinance will return for a second reading and adoption at the next regular City
  Council meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS (TIME LIMITATION - 5 MINUTES)
Citizens wishing to address the Council on any matter which is within the subject matter
jurisdiction of the City Council not on the Agenda may do so at this time. Please note that while
the City Council values your comments, pursuant to the Brown Act, the City Council cannot take
action unless the matter appears as an item on a forthcoming agenda.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS) F2M23-7
Each Councilmember at his/her discretion may address the Council and public on matters of
general information and/or concern, including announcements and future agenda items.

ADJOURNMENT: The next regular meeting of the Alhambra City Council is scheduled for
Monday, November 13, 2023 at 6:00 p.m.
  NOTICE
Agenda Items: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to the items listed
on this agenda are on file with the City Clerk in Alhambra City Hall, located at 111 South First Street,
Alhambra, California, and are available for inspection during regular office hours, Monday through
Thursday from 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. or please call (626) 570-5090. If you would like to sign-up to
receive the City Council meeting agenda and staff reports packet, please visit the City’s website at
www.cityofalhambra.org and you will be able to submit your email address on the homepage to the
subscription service. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.5(b), materials related to agenda
items for regular meetings of the Alhambra City Council that are distributed less than 72 hours prior to
that meeting, will be made available for public inspection at the Alhambra City Clerk’s Office.
  10
10-23-23
 Broadcast of Meeting: A live video stream of each Council meeting is available through the City’s
website. The regular meetings of the Alhambra City Council are recorded and are broadcast on
Charter Channels 3 and 182 at 7:30 p.m. on Thursdays and Mondays following the meeting.
Recordings are also available for viewing by the public on the City of Alhambra’s website, at the
Alhambra Public Library and, upon appointment, in the City Clerk’s Office.

Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City meeting
(including assisted listening devices), please contact the City Clerk's Office at (626) 570-5090.
Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable
arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

Translation Services Requests: If you require translation services in order to participate in a meeting

        10 DAY REPORT ON THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA’S TEMPORARY MORATORIUM
ON THE ISSUANCE OF ENTITLEMENTS AND PERMITS FOR THE
ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW FIREARM SALES BUSINESSES IN THE CITY

BACKGROUND

On September 25th, 2023, the City Council adopted AN URGENCY ORDINANCE OF THE
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA, CALIFORNIA, ENACTED
PURSUANT TO CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65858, ADOPTING
AN INTERIM ZONING ORDINANCE TEMPORARILY PROHIBITING THE
ESTABLISHMENT OF NEW FIREARM SALES BUSINESSES IN THE CITY.

As detailed in the Ordinance and accompanying staff report, the Council has expressed some
concern about the potential proliferation of new firearm retail businesses, based upon firearm
purchasing trends, the fact that Monterey Park has adopted geographic restrictions on the
establishment of new firearms retailers in their city and the fact that enquiries have been made
about potential sites for new firearms businesses in the City of Alhambra.

UPDATE ON THE MEASURES TAKEN TO ALLEVIATE THE CONDITIONS THAT LED
TO THE ADOPTION OF THE URGENCY ORDINANCE
1.  City staff intends to further research the impacts on the City and its various
neighborhoods of the establishment of additional firearm retail businesses.

2.  Staff plans to research potential regulations that could address the impacts identified after
further study. This could include the identification of areas where such uses may be
inappropriate due to nearby sensitive uses.

3.  After concluding the research and development of alternatives, staff intends to prepare
revised regulations for such businesses, possible with further direction from the Council.

4.  Once proposed permanent regulations are developed, staff intends to take a permanent
ordinance with proposed standards to the Planning Commission for public hearing and review,
and then to the City Council.

5.  An extension of the interim ordinance is needed to accommodate the processing of a
permanent ordinance. The extension will be for a period of ten (10) months and fifteen (15) days
or until a permanent change to the interim ordinance is adopted, whichever comes first.

2.  CONSIDER ADOPTION OF AN URGENCY INTERIM ZONING ORDINANCE EXTENDING

  FIREARM SALES BUSINESSES AND DETERMINE THIS ACTION IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA –
  F2M23-7, N2M23-124, O2M23-4818, O2M23-4821

  City Attorney MONTES delivered a staff report. This is the time and place set by Notice No.
  N2M23-124 for the City Council to hold a public hearing to consider adoption of an urgency interim
  zoning ordinance extending Ordinance No. O2M23-4818, the prohibition on the establishment of
  new firearm sales businesses. At the September 25, 2023 City Council meeting, the City Council
  adopted Ordinance No. O2M23-4818 imposing a 45-day moratorium on the establishment of new
  retail firearm sales businesses in the City. The reasoning behind and need for such ordinance is
  set forth in the September 25, 2023 staff report and ordinance. Staff requires additional time to
  study the “buffer” ordinance that Monterey Park adopted and evaluate its suitability for the City of
  Alhambra, then prepare a recommendation to the Planning Commission, and ultimately the City
  Council. California Government Code section 65858 allows for the adoption of interim zoning
  regulations, including moratorium ordinances, on an urgency basis to preserve the health, safety
  and welfare of the residents of Alhambra by maintaining the status quo while research and analysis
  is undertaken to develop appropriate regulations to discuss these concerns. An initial ordinance
  can be adopted to last 45 days. Thereafter, the ordinance can be extended, if needed, for a period
  of ten months and 15 days. This ordinance would extend the current ordinance to and through
  September 24, 2024. If permanent regulations are adopted prior to the expiration of the extended
  moratorium, it can be repealed at that time.

  The City reviewed the environmental impacts of this extension Ordinance under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the regulations
  promulgated thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). This
  Ordinances is not subject to further review environmental review because: (1) it will not result in a
  direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs.
  § 15060(c)(2); (2) there is no possibility that the Ordinance itself may have a significant effect on
  the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15061(b)(3)); and (3) the Ordinance, by itself, does not
  constitute a “project” as defined in the CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15378). The
  Ordinance is for general policies and procedure-making.

  Opened Public Hearing: Mayor MAZA opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St., expressed support for the urgency
  ordinance.

  Closed Public Hearing: After receiving public testimony, Mayor MAZA closed the public hearing.

19.  FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE EXTENDING THE TERM OF ORDINANCE NO.
  O2M23-4812, A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON CERTAIN “NO FAULT”
  RESIDENTIAL EVICTIONS DUE TO A PROPERTY OWNER’S INTENT TO
  SUBSTANTIALLY REMODEL THE TENANT’S UNIT IN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA AND
  DETERMINE THIS ACTION IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA – F2M23-7, O2M23-4812, O2M23-
  4822

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M23-4812, imposing a
  temporary moratorium on so called “renovictions,” through December 31, 2023. On
  September 30, 2023, SB 567 was signed by the Governor. SB 567 revises certain tenant
  11
10-23-23
   protections in State law which address the concerns that the City’s moratorium was intended
  to address. However, those protections do not take effect until April 1, 2024. At the October
  9, 2023 City Council meeting, the City Council directed that an amendment to Ordinance
  No. O2M23-4812 be agendized to extend the term of the temporary moratorium on
  renovictions until the tenant protections of SB 567 become effective. The City reviewed the
  environmental impacts of this Ordinance under the California Environmental Quality Act
  (Public Resources Code §§ 21000, et seq. “CEQA”) and the regulations promulgated
  thereunder (14 Cal. Code of Regs. §§ 15000, et seq., the “CEQA Guidelines”). This Ordinance
  is not subject to further review environmental review because: (1) it will not result in a direct
  or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs.
  § 15060(c)(2); (2) there is no possibility that this Ordinance themselves may have a
  significant effect on the environment (14 Cal. Code Regs. § 15061(b)(3)); and (3) the
  Ordinance, by itself, do not constitute a “project” as defined in the CEQA Guidelines (14 Cal.
  Code Regs. § 15378). The Ordinance is for general policies and procedure-making.

  Public Comment:  Ho Sun PHAM expressed opposition to the temporary moratorium
ordinance.

  City Attorney MONTES briefly responded to the public comment.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor PÉREZ recommended providing education material regarding SB
  567 for local property owners.

  Action Taken:  Declared introduced for its first reading the following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M23-4822: An Ordinance of the City Council of the
  City of Alhambra, California, extending the term of Ordinance No.
  O2M23-4812, a temporary Moratorium on certain “no fault” residential
  evictions due to a property owner’s intent to substantially remodel the
  tenant’s unit in the City of Alhambra

  which ordinance would return for a second reading and adoption at the next regular City
  Council meeting.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
